newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics down on SFC speculation check.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics down on SFC speculation check.

text.p: Taiwan's trendsetting electronics shares slipped in early Wednesday trade after the watchdog Securities and Futures Commission said it had launched a routine investigation on credit trading in the stock market.
The commission denied the move aimed to cool down the red hot stock market.
After 38 minutes, at 0138 GMT, the electronics sector was down 0.25 percent, though recovered from a 0.99 percent dip, while the overall index was up 0.37 percent.
Leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor was down T$2 or 1.64 percent to T$120.
Brokers said any impact from the check would be felt most by electronics, which accounted for much of the recent turnover.
"Since electronics account for some 60 percent of the market turnover, the SFC check surely will hit that sector most," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
"But bargain hunters have kept on coming for electronics, so its seems investors confidence on the sector remains strong despite the SFC move," Yang said.
A commission official said credit trading -- including margin loan buying and short selling -- had accounted for some 55 percent of the market's daily turnover recently.
"Intraday credit trading (previously) had accounted for 25-30 percent of credit trading, indicating speculation is strengthening," the official said.
